chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Rib'i from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the testimony of a woman who witnessed a man making a will, with no man accompanying her, he said: 'One-quarter of what he bequeathed is accepted based on her testimony.'
ai.seo_question: What is the value of a woman's testimony in Islamic inheritance law when she witnesses a will alone?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details a specific legal nuance where a woman’s testimony, in the absence of a male witness, validates only one-quarter of the bequeathed amount, reflecting the classical juristic principle that one female witness equals half a male witness. It highlights the practical application of this ratio in inheritance law, demonstrating how Shia scholars derived precise financial valuations from prophetic traditions to resolve evidentiary gaps in will-making.
